Emberfall

a guide to the world, written by the world

Emberfall is an old world and an unhelpful one. Nothing marks your quest on the map, nothing carries you between towns, and when you die your body stays where it fell with everything you owned still on it. You begin in Emberhold at level 1 and you reach level 50 on foot.

There are 45 zones across 7 realms, every one of them built and open. Six realms each belong to one of the elephant gods, and the deeper you walk into one the less it resembles anywhere you have been.

Starting Out

Making a character

10 races, 8 classes, 40 legal pairings

Choose the race first. It decides the city you wake up in, who draws a sword when you walk through a gate, and which classes will take you at all — not every class is open to every race.

Every stat starts at 75 before your race touches it. You then have 25 points to place, and no more than 15 of them may go into any single stat.

Races10
Classes8
Legal pairings40
Every stat begins at75
Points to place25
Most into one stat15

Levels and experience

The cap is 50

Experience comes from what you kill, weighted by its level. Something a little above you pays best; something far below you pays almost nothing, so there is no farming the first zone to fifty.

In a group everyone earns as long as the highest and lowest members are within 10 levels. Outside that gap the low character is simply being carried.

Until level 15 you carry the Elders’ Blessing and earn 15% more.

The climb steepens. Up to level 10 a level is about the same number of kills as the last; past that, each level asks 6.7% more again for every level beyond it — so level 25 is about 2.0× the work of level 10, and level 50 about 3.7×.

Level cap50
Group level gap10
Elders’ Blessing+15% to level 15

Dying

It costs you, and then it costs you the walk back

Death takes 10% of the experience you had earned toward your next level. Your corpse stays where you fell, holding everything you were carrying, and you wake at your bind point with nothing. Getting your things back means walking to the body.

Bind yourself at a bindstone in a city before you travel. That stone is where you reappear, and how far it is from where you died is the real penalty.

A corpse lasts 60 minutes.

Experience lost10%
Corpse lasts60 min
Back on your feet after4.0 sec

Getting about

On foot, mostly

Roads run between zones and a zone line is a place on the ground you walk across. There is no map marker to click.

A Pathcaller stands in eight of the cities — Barrowhold, Duskhold, Emberhold, Forgehold, Galehold, Lanternhold, Murkhold and Rainhold — and will call the road to anywhere you have already walked to yourself. Not the Grove, not a room indoors, not a dungeon, and not while something is fighting you. The first journey anywhere is always on foot.

The road is priced by where it goes: a zone’s top level squared, times 4 copper. 1 gold, 9 silver and 6 copper to Greenmoor, 10 platinum to Timiraj's Table. Another city is a flat 1 platinum.

Sprinting is 1.55 times walking pace and drains stamina, of which you have 100 at level 1 and 4 more each level. Run it dry and you walk until it returns.

You can carry 60 stone, plus 3 a level and 3 for each point of strength. Coin has weight, which is why bankers exist.

Sprint1.55× walking
Stamina at level 1100
Stamina a level+4
Carried weight60
Bag slots24
Bank slots16

Who trusts you

Every city and every warband keeps its own tally

Kill something and several tallies move at once: the thing’s kin think worse of you and its enemies think better. At -1500 a faction is hostile and its guards attack on sight.

Your race sets the opening position. The good cities are Citizens of Emberhold, The Watch, Citizens of Lanternhold, Forgehold, Citizens of Galehold, Pilgrims of the Dawn and Fishers of Hollowmere; the evil ones are Citizens of Murkhold and Citizens of Duskhold. An evil race begins hostile to the good side and a good or neutral race to the evil side. Everyone not on a side — traders, hermits, the neutral holds — begins indifferent and can be won round.

Some classes carry their own reputation: a necromancer starts -300 with the good cities.

City guards are not a fight you win. They stand at level 70, 10× the health and 3× the damage of an ordinary monster that far above you.

A race is the one choice you cannot undo. It places you on the map, sets the five stats you will build on for fifty levels, decides which classes will have you, and tells every city guard in the world whether to nod or draw.

Classes

Eight trades, and the one you pick decides how a fight feels for fifty levels: whether you stand in front of it, heal the person who does, or make sure it never reaches either of you. Health, mana and armour below are what the class gives you before a single piece of gear goes on.

Gods

Nine elephant gods, and you choose one when you make a character. Five of them hold a realm on the map and the rest are older or stranger than that. What a god gives you is small and permanent: a little more health, a little more mana, a lighter death. What they ask is nothing, which should worry you.

Four of the nine will not take an evil race. The rest do not care what you are.

Prabhagaj

the Dawn-Tusk, over The Dawnstair

The elephant of first light. Nothing is hidden from him for long, and what he shows you, you have to look at.

Grants Wounds close faster: +1 hit point regeneration.

Takes Good and neutral races only, so not Dark Elf, Troll and Ogre.

RealmThe Dawnstair
Its levels1–24
Its zones7
Health regained a tick+1

Jalendra

the Tide-Trunked, over The Long Monsoon

She keeps the rivers and the rain. The water has already made room for you; that is the only welcome she gives, and the only one she means.

Grants A deeper well: +10% maximum mana.

Takes Good and neutral races only, so not Dark Elf, Troll and Ogre.

the Unlit, over The Boneyard

The place elephants go at the end. He remembers every one who falls, which is not the comfort it sounds like.

Grants Remembered: dying costs half the experience.

Takes Anyone at all, whatever their race or reputation.

Makarosh

the Deep-Jawed, with no realm of their own on the map

The crocodile beneath the black water. He waits longer than anything alive, and everything that drinks from the bog drinks from his mouth. His faithful learn to be still.

Grants Still as the deep: monsters notice you 10% later.

Takes Only Troll and Ogre.

Realmnone on the map
How soon a monster notices you-10%

Mahishra

the Mud-Horned, with no realm of their own on the map

The great buffalo who churned the first mud out of the world's floor. He is strength that doesn't hurry, and he despises anything that runs.

Grants Hide like the herd's: +5% maximum health.

Takes Only Troll and Ogre.

Realmnone on the map
Maximum health+5%

Tantuvi

the Many-Eyed, with no realm of their own on the map

She weaves the webs between the stars, and every strand she spins is a thread of someone's fate. Her faithful learn that anything can be caught, given time.

Grants Slow poison: your damage over time hits 10% harder.

Takes Only Dark Elf.

Realmnone on the map
Damage over time+10%

Dipanti

the Lamp-Eater, with no realm of their own on the map

Drawn to every light, and she puts each one out. Duskhold's candles are prayers to her, and bait. What she takes from the flame, she gives to her faithful.

Grants Stolen light: +8% maximum mana.

Takes Only Dark Elf.

Skills

A skill goes up by using it, and how high it can go depends on your class and your level: the cap is a little higher every level until it reaches 100. The number below is the level at which a class finally holds that skill at 100 — lower is better, and a dash means the class never learns it at all.

Nothing here is a choice you make. You raise a skill by swinging, casting, hiding or cooking, and the cap is what stops you running ahead of your level.

Tradeskillsopen to everyone

Cooking, Tailoring, Alchemy and Smithing are not gated by class or level. Anyone can raise any of them to 100; the only thing in your way is practice and materials.

Quests

345 tasks, under the town or the wilderness where the person who wants them stands. Nobody has a mark over their head: you hail them, and you ask about the thing in brackets. The words to say are printed with each task.

158 of them can be done again, for 50% of the experience the first time paid. The item a task hands over is given once.

Items

Everything you can pick up, 1035 of them, under the place it goes or the reason you carry it. Where an item comes from is printed with it: what drops it, who asks for it, and which shop keeps one.

322 are marked never leaves you: once it is yours it cannot be traded, sold or left on a corpse for someone else.

Where a weapon has a picture, that is the model the game puts in your hand — rendered from the same file the game loads. Weapons share their models, so every arming sword in the world looks like the one beside Rusty Short Sword, because in the game it does.

In hand141

Rusty DaggerSold by Tea-Seller Moti in Dewstep.

183 of them are named: a named creature throws away its own health and takes the typical health of its level 2 times over, so the numbers here are what you will actually fight. 62 have had their portrait taken so far.

Zones

45 zones, laid out on a grid you can walk across without a loading screen asking your permission. Each one names the zones it borders and which way you leave to reach them; follow those far enough in any direction and you will run out of world.

Level ranges are what the zone is built for, not a wall. Nothing stops you walking into the Boneyard at level 6 except what lives there.
